;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Darfur]]
**[[2020 Darfur attacks]]
***At least 20 people are killed and 22 others wounded in a [[mass shooting]] in a village in [[South Darfur]], [[Sudan]]. [https://ca.reuters.com/article/topNews/idCAKCN24Q0JJ (Reuters)]
*[[American-led intervention in Iraq (2014–2021)]]
**[[Combined Joint Task Force – Operation Inherent Resolve|CJTF–OIR]] hands over control of [[Besmaya Range Complex]] in [[Baghdad Governorate]], which houses [[Spanish Army|Spanish troops]], to [[Iraqi security forces]]. It is the seventh military base to be handed over to Iraqi forces since the beginning of the [[Withdrawal of U.S. troops from Iraq (2020)|withdrawal of U.S. and coalition troops]]. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-07/25/c_139239948.htm (Xinhua)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[2020 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**[[Hurricane Hanna (2020)|Hurricane Hanna]]
***Tropical Storm Hanna is upgraded to a [[hurricane]] and heads toward the [[Texas]] coast, threatening to bring heavy rain, storm surge and possible tornadoes. Hanna is reported as the first hurricane of the 2020 Atlantic hurricane season by the U.S. National Hurricane Center. [https://apnews.com/9ad8058b3e666cf8b3f93b7ceb2ee1c4 (AP)]
*Three people are killed when a [[microlight aircraft]] crashes into a home in [[Wesel]], [[North Rhine-Westphalia|NRW]], [[Germany]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-53539010 (BBC News)]
*Four people are killed when a small plane crashes in [[Blatten (Lötschen)|Blatten]], [[Canton of Valais|Valais]], [[Switzerland]]. [https://www.ilmessaggero.it/mondo/morti_quattro_aereo_precipitato_svizzera_cantone_vallese-5367738.html (''Il Messaggero'')]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong]]
****Hong Kong reports a record of 133 new cases of COVID-19 for the fourth consecutive day, as well as two deaths. 126 of these cases are locally transmitted. [https://www.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/health-environment/article/3094681/hong-kong-third-wave-elderly-man-becomes-citys (''South China Morning Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****[[South Korea]] reports 113 new cases of COVID-19. This is the largest one-day increase since March. Of these new cases, 86 were imported and 27 were locally transmitted. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2020/07/25/asia-pacific/south-korea-reports-113-coronavirus/ (''The Japan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]]
****[[Vietnam]] confirms its first case of COVID-19 community transmission in 100 days. A patient is a 57-year-old man in [[Da Nang]] who had no prior contact with any known cases. [https://e.vnexpress.net/news/news/vietnam-confirms-first-case-of-COVID-19-community-transmission-in-100-days-4135963.html (VnExpress)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Qatar]]
****Retired [[association football|footballer]] and current coach of [[Al Sadd SC]] [[Xavi|Xavi Hernández]] announces he tested positive for COVID-19. [https://www.forbes.com/sites/tomsanderson/2020/07/25/fc-barcelona-legend-xavi-tests-positive-for-covid-19/ (''Forbes'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in North Korea]]
****[[Kim Jong-un]] convenes an emergency meeting of the [[Central Committee of the Workers' Party of Korea]], declares a [[state of emergency]], and orders the lockdown of [[Kaesong]] after a person suspected of having COVID-19 returned from [[South Korea]], after illegally crossing the [[Korean Demilitarized Zone|DMZ]]. If confirmed, it would be the first time a case of COVID-19 has been officially acknowledged by North Korea. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-northkorea-idUSKCN24Q0TC (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Florida]]
****[[Florida]] surpasses [[New York (state)|New York]], once the epicenter of the pandemic, to hold the second highest number of COVID-19 cases in the United States, with a total 414,511 confirmed cases. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/07/25/health/us-coronavirus-saturday/index.html (CNN)]

;Law and crime
*[[George Floyd protests]]
**[[George Floyd protests in Seattle]]
***Forty-five people are arrested after protesters throw explosives and rocks at police in [[Seattle]]. Other rioters set fire to a portable trailer and a construction site, police allege in a series of tweets. Twenty-one [[Seattle Police Department|officers]] were injured, including one who was hospitalized with a leg injury caused by an explosive. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/07/25/us/seattle-protest-riot/index.html (CNN)]
**[[George Floyd protests in Texas]]
***During an evening  protest in [[Austin, Texas]], a man is fatally shot  as he approached a vehicle and the driver inside opened fire. A police spokesperson says the victim may have been carrying a rifle. She added that the suspect was detained and is cooperating with police. [https://www.dallasnews.com/news/texas/2020/07/26/man-fatally-shot-at-protest-in-austin/ (AP via ''Dallas Morning News'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Central African general election|2020 Central African Republic general election]]
**Deposed [[President of the Central African Republic|president]] [[François Bozizé]] announces his bid for the presidency, despite being the subject of sanctions by the [[United Nations]] and an [[arrest warrant]], issued by the current government, for alleged [[crimes against humanity]]. The Central African Republic has been in [[Central African Republic Civil War (2012–present)|a civil war]] between [[Muslim]]s and [[Christians]] since he was deposed in 2013. It is not known whether the charges against him will play a role in his candidacy. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-centralafrica-vote-bozize/deposed-central-african-republic-leader-announces-presidential-bid-idUSKCN24Q0O4?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[2020 Thai protests]], [[LGBT rights in Thailand]]
**An [[LGBT]] group gathers at the [[Democracy Monument]], [[Bangkok]], to call for legalization of [[same-sex marriage]] in addition to the three demands stated by Free Youths. [https://prachatai.com/journal/2020/07/88756 (''Prachatai'')]
*The [[Parliament of Somalia]] conducts a [[no-confidence vote]] of 170–8 to oust [[Prime Minister of Somalia|Prime Minister]] [[Hassan Ali Khaire]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-somalia-politics/somalias-parliament-votes-to-oust-pm-hassan-ali-khaire-idUSKCN24Q0EW?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Science and technology
*[[Global warming]]
**A record high temperature of 21.7[[Celsius|°C]] (71.1[[Fahrenheit|°F]]) is recorded on the [[Arctic]] archipelago of [[Svalbard]], according to the [[Norwegian Meteorological Institute]]. [https://globalnews.ca/news/7217861/norway-arctic-archipelago-warming/ (Global News)]
